    44:         ansible.builtin.combine(adf_app_configuration, recursive=true)

    18:       shell: >-

    20:         --format "{% raw %}{{.Names}}|||{{.Image}}|||{{.Ports}}{% endraw %}"

    22:       register: running_containers_raw
    23:       changed_when: false

    26:     - name: Build aqa_containers data structure
    27:       vars:
    28:         # Each line: "<name>|||<image>|||<ports>"
    29:         # e.g. "U2404.32001|||aqa_u2404|||0.0.0.0:32001->22/tcp"
    30:         parsed: >-
    31:           {{
    32:             running_containers_raw.stdout_lines
    33:             | map('split', '|||')
    34:             | list
    35:           }}
    36:         # Strip registry prefix, aqa_ prefix, .arm32 suffix, and :tag suffix
    37:         image_suffix: >-
    38:           {{
    39:             item[1] | regex_replace('^(localhost/)?aqa_', '')
    40:                     | regex_replace('\.arm32$', '')

    51:                             else item[0].split('.')[-1],

     2: # This playbook shrinks Ceph OSDs that have been created with ceph-volume.

     4: #
     5: # Use it like this:
     6: # ansible-playbook shrink-osd.yml -e osd_to_kill=0,2,6
     7: #     Prompts for confirmation to shrink, defaults to no and
     8: #     doesn't shrink the cluster. yes shrinks the cluster.
     9: #
    10: # ansible-playbook -e ireallymeanit=yes|no shrink-osd.yml
    11: #     Overrides the prompt using -e option. Can be used in
    12: #     automation scripts to avoid interactive prompt.
    13: 
    14: - name: Gather facts and check the init system
    15:   hosts:
    16:     - mons
    17:     - osds
    18: 
    19:   become: true
    20:   tasks:
    21:     - name: Gather facts on all Ceph hosts for following reference
    22:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    23:         msg: "gather facts on all Ceph hosts for following reference"
    24: 
    25: - name: Confirm whether user really meant to remove osd(s) from the cluster
    26:   hosts: mons[0]
    27:   become: true
    28:   vars_prompt:
    29:     - name: ireallymeanit  # noqa: name[casing]
    30:       prompt: Are you sure you want to shrink the cluster?
    31:       default: 'no'
    32:       private: false
    33:   vars:
    34:     mon_group_name: mons
    35:     osd_group_name: osds
    36: 
    37:   pre_tasks:
    38:     - name: Exit playbook, if user did not mean to shrink cluster
    39:       ansible.builtin.fail:

    41:            To shrink the cluster, either say 'yes' on the prompt or
    42:            or use `-e ireallymeanit=yes` on the command line when
    43:            invoking the playbook"
    44:       when: ireallymeanit != 'yes'
    45: 
    46:     - name: Exit playbook, if no osd(s) was/were given

    50:            On the command line when invoking the playbook, you can use
    51:            -e osd_to_kill=0,1,2,3 argument."
    52:       when: osd_to_kill is not defined
    53: 
    54:     - name: Check the osd ids passed have the correct format

    59: 
    60:   tasks:

    63:         name: ceph-defaults
    64: 
    65:     - name: Import ceph-facts role

    67:         name: ceph-facts
    68:         tasks_from: container_binary
    69: 
    70:   post_tasks:

    72:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    73:         container_exec_cmd: "{{ container_binary }} exec ceph-mon-{{ ansible_facts['hostname'] }}"

    76:     - name: Exit playbook, if can not connect to the cluster

    79:       changed_when: false

    82:       delay: 2

    84:     - name: Find the host(s) where the osd(s) is/are running on
    85:       ansible.builtin.command: "{{ container_exec_cmd }} ceph --cluster {{ cluster }} osd find {{ item }}"
    86:       changed_when: false

    89: 
    90:     - name: Set_fact osd_hosts

    92:         osd_hosts: "{{ osd_hosts | default([]) + [[(item.stdout | from_json).crush_location.host, (item.stdout | from_json).osd_fsid, item.item]] }}"
    93:       with_items: "{{ find_osd_hosts.results }}"
    94: 
    95:     - name: Set_fact _osd_hosts
    96:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    97:         _osd_hosts: "{{ _osd_hosts | default([]) + [ [ item.0, item.2, item.3 ] ] }}"
    98:       with_nested:
    99:         - "{{ groups.get(osd_group_name) }}"
   100:         - "{{ osd_hosts }}"

   107: 
   108:     - name: Get ceph-volume lvm list data

   111:         action: list
   112:       environment:
   113:         CEPH_CONTAINER_IMAGE: "{{ ceph_docker_registry + '/' + ceph_docker_image + ':' + ceph_docker_image_tag if containerized_deployment | bool else '' }}"

   127:         force: true

   132:     - name: Get osd unit status

   134:         name: ceph-osd@{{ item.2 }}

   138:       when:

   141:     - name: Refresh /etc/ceph/osd files containerized_deployment
   142:       ansible.builtin.command: "{{ container_binary }} exec ceph-osd-{{ item.2 }} ceph-volume simple scan --force /var/lib/ceph/osd/{{ cluster }}-{{ item.2 }}"
   143:       changed_when: false

   145:       loop: "{{ _osd_hosts }}"

   150: 
   151:     - name: Refresh /etc/ceph/osd files containerized_deployment when OSD container is down
   152:       when:
   153:         - containerized_deployment | bool
   154:         - osd_status.results[0].status.ActiveState != 'active'
   155:       block:
   156:         - name: Create tmp osd folder
   157:           ansible.builtin.file:
   158:             path: /var/lib/ceph/tmp/{{ cluster }}-{{ item.2 }}

   160:             mode: '0755'
   161:           delegate_to: "{{ item.0 }}"
   162:           when: item.2 not in _lvm_list.keys()
   163:           loop: "{{ _osd_hosts }}"
   164: 
   165:         - name: Activate OSD
   166:           ansible.builtin.command: |
   167:             {{ container_binary }} run -ti --pids-limit=-1 --rm --net=host --privileged=true --pid=host --ipc=host --cpus=1
   168:             -v /dev:/dev -v /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
   169:             -v /var/lib/ceph/tmp/:/var/lib/ceph/osd:z,rshared
   170:             -v /etc/ceph:/etc/ceph:z -v /var/run/ceph:/var/run/ceph:z
   171:             -v /var/run/udev/:/var/run/udev/ -v /var/log/ceph:/var/log/ceph:z
   172:             -e OSD_BLUESTORE=1 -e OSD_FILESTORE=0 -e OSD_DMCRYPT=0 -e CLUSTER=ceph -e DEBUG=verbose
   173:             -e TCMALLOC_MAX_TOTAL_THREAD_CACHE_BYTES=134217728 -v /run/lvm/:/run/lvm/
   174:             -e CEPH_DAEMON=OSD_CEPH_VOLUME_ACTIVATE -e CONTAINER_IMAGE={{ ceph_docker_registry + '/' + ceph_docker_image + ':' + ceph_docker_image_tag }}
   175:             -e OSD_ID={{ item.2 }}

   178:             simple activate {{ item.2 }} {{ item.1 }} --no-systemd

   180:           delegate_to: "{{ item.0 }}"
   181:           when: item.2 not in _lvm_list.keys()
   182:           loop: "{{ _osd_hosts }}"
   183: 
   184:         - name: Simple scan
   185:           ansible.builtin.command: |
   186:             {{ container_binary }} run -ti --pids-limit=-1 --rm --net=host --privileged=true --pid=host --ipc=host --cpus=1
   187:             -v /dev:/dev -v /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro

   189:             -v /etc/ceph:/etc/ceph:z -v /var/run/ceph:/var/run/ceph:z

   191:             -e OSD_BLUESTORE=1 -e OSD_FILESTORE=0 -e OSD_DMCRYPT=0 -e CLUSTER=ceph -e DEBUG=verbose

   193:             -e CEPH_DAEMON=OSD_CEPH_VOLUME_ACTIVATE -e CONTAINER_IMAGE={{ ceph_docker_registry + '/' + ceph_docker_image + ':' + ceph_docker_image_tag }}
   194:             -e OSD_ID={{ item.2 }}
   195:             --entrypoint=ceph-volume
   196:             {{ ceph_docker_registry + '/' + ceph_docker_image + ':' + ceph_docker_image_tag }}
   197:             simple scan --force /var/lib/ceph/osd/{{ cluster }}-{{ item.2 }}
   198:           changed_when: false
   199:           delegate_to: "{{ item.0 }}"
   200:           when: item.2 not in _lvm_list.keys()
   201:           loop: "{{ _osd_hosts }}"
   202: 
   203:         - name: Umount OSD temp folder
   204:           ansible.posix.mount:
   205:             path: /var/lib/ceph/tmp/{{ cluster }}-{{ item.2 }}

   208:           when: item.2 not in _lvm_list.keys()
   209:           loop: "{{ _osd_hosts }}"

   244:     - name: Mark osd(s) out of the cluster

   297: 
   298:     - name: Close dmcrypt close on devices if needed

   312:

   336:       environment:

   338:         CEPH_CONTAINER_IMAGE: "{{ ceph_docker_registry + '/' + ceph_docker_image + ':' + ceph_docker_image_tag if containerized_deployment | bool else '' }}"

    58:       GID: "{{ minecraft_game_gid }}"
    59:       MEMORY: "{{ minecraft_game_memory }}"

    61:       DIFFICULTY: "normal"
    62:       MAX_PLAYERS: "20"
    63:       MOTD: "California | Java | Survival"

    65:       # under any name, including the names in the whitelist below.

    74:       ENABLE_WHITELIST: "true"
    75:       ENFORCE_WHITELIST: "true"

    94: # --- Nightly world backup (issue #565) -------------------------------------

    97: # directory, is in the docker group (so `docker exec ... rcon-cli` works) and

    99: # written. That keeps a `--tags minecraft` run sudo-free on an appliance with

   113:     mode: "0755"

   136:     minute: "{{ minecraft_game_backup_minute }}"
   137:     hour: "{{ minecraft_game_backup_hour }}"

    18: # so installing it means `dpkg --add-architecture i386` — a system-wide change that doubles apt

name: roles/ssl/tasks/build_certificate_chain.yml

1: ---
     2: # Certificate Chain Building Tasks
     3: # --------------------------------
     4: # Inputs:
     5: #   - ca_cert_path: PEM file containing one or more trusted CA certificates
     6: #     (root and/or intermediate, in any order).
     7: #   - cert_path: PEM file containing the signed server certificate.
     8: #     May be leaf-only or include any subset of intermediates and/or the root,
     9: #     in any order.
    10: #
    11: # Output:
    12: #   - {{ ssl_file_dir_final }}/{{ service_name }}.chain — properly ordered
    13: #     "leaf -> intermediate(s) -> root" chain. For partial chains where no
    14: #     self-signed root is available, the walk stops at the topmost cert that
    15: #     has a known parent in the trust pool.
    16: #
    17: # Algorithm:
    18: #   1. Split both ca_cert_path and cert_path into individual cert files.
    19: #   2. Identify the leaf in cert_path: the cert whose Subject is not the
    20: #      Issuer of any other cert in cert_path (handles arbitrary input order).
    21: #   3. Use the non-leaf certs from cert_path as -untrusted bridges and run a
    22: #      single `openssl verify -CAfile <bundle> -untrusted <bridges>
    23: #      -partial_chain <leaf>`. This validates the chain cryptographically and
    24: #      handles DoD-style partial chains via -partial_chain.
    25: #   4. Walk Issuer -> Subject across the union of all certs (cert_path +
    26: #      ca_cert_path), starting from the leaf, to emit the ordered chain.
    27: #      OpenSSL has already proven the chain is valid; the walk only sorts
    28: #      the certs into output order.
    29: 
    30: - name: Create temp directory for individual certificates
    31:   tempfile:
    32:     state: directory
    33:     suffix: cert_chain
    34:   register: temp_dir
    35: 
    36: - name: Build and Verify Certificate Chain
    37:   shell: |
    38:     set -euo pipefail
    39: 
    40:     TEMP_DIR='{{ temp_dir.path }}'
    41:     CA_CERT_PATH='{{ ca_cert_path }}'
    42:     CERT_PATH='{{ cert_path }}'
    43:     OUTPUT_CHAIN='{{ ssl_file_dir_final }}/{{ service_name }}.chain'
    44: 
    45:     # 1. Split both input files into individual cert files. The `n>0` gate
    46:     #    drops any leading lines (whitespace, comments, BOM) before the first
    47:     #    BEGIN CERTIFICATE marker so the glob does not pick up junk files.
    48:     awk 'BEGIN{n=0} /BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{n++} n>0 {print > ("'"$TEMP_DIR"'/cert."n".pem")}' "$CERT_PATH"
    49:     awk 'BEGIN{n=0} /BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{n++} n>0 {print > ("'"$TEMP_DIR"'/ca."n".pem")}'   "$CA_CERT_PATH"
    50: 
    51:     cert_files=( "$TEMP_DIR"/cert.*.pem )
    52:     ca_files=(   "$TEMP_DIR"/ca.*.pem )
    53:     if [ ! -e "${cert_files[0]}" ]; then
    54:       echo "ERROR: no certificates found in cert_path ($CERT_PATH)" >&2
    55:       exit 1
    56:     fi
    57:     if [ ! -e "${ca_files[0]}" ]; then
    58:       echo "ERROR: no certificates found in ca_cert_path ($CA_CERT_PATH)" >&2
    59:       exit 1
    60:     fi
    61: 
    62:     subj_of() { openssl x509 -in "$1" -noout -subject -nameopt RFC2253 | sed 's/^subject=//'; }
    63:     iss_of()  { openssl x509 -in "$1" -noout -issuer  -nameopt RFC2253 | sed 's/^issuer=//';  }
    64: 
    65:     # 2. Identify the leaf in cert_path:
    66:     #    the cert whose Subject is NOT the Issuer of any other cert in cert_path.
    67:     LEAF=""
    68:     for f in "${cert_files[@]}"; do
    69:       f_subj=$(subj_of "$f")
    70:       is_parent=false
    71:       for g in "${cert_files[@]}"; do
    72:         [ "$g" = "$f" ] && continue
    73:         if [ "$(iss_of "$g")" = "$f_subj" ]; then
    74:           is_parent=true
    75:           break
    76:         fi
    77:       done
    78:       if ! $is_parent; then
    79:         LEAF="$f"
    80:         break
    81:       fi
    82:     done
    83:     if [ -z "$LEAF" ]; then
    84:       echo "ERROR: could not identify leaf certificate in cert_path ($CERT_PATH)" >&2
    85:       exit 1
    86:     fi
    87: 
    88:     # 3. Collect non-leaf certs from cert_path as bridging intermediates.
    89:     BRIDGES="$TEMP_DIR/bridges.pem"
    90:     : > "$BRIDGES"
    91:     for f in "${cert_files[@]}"; do
    92:       [ "$f" = "$LEAF" ] && continue
    93:       cat "$f" >> "$BRIDGES"
    94:     done
    95: 
    96:     # 4. Verify the chain. -partial_chain permits stopping at a trusted
    97:     #    intermediate (DoD/enterprise PKI without root in the bundle).
    98:     if [ -s "$BRIDGES" ]; then
    99:       openssl verify -CAfile "$CA_CERT_PATH" -untrusted "$BRIDGES" -partial_chain "$LEAF" >&2
   100:     else
   101:       openssl verify -CAfile "$CA_CERT_PATH" -partial_chain "$LEAF" >&2
   102:     fi
   103: 
   104:     # 5. Walk Issuer -> Subject across all available certs to emit the chain
   105:     #    in leaf -> intermediate(s) -> root order. Dedupe by Subject (one cert
   106:     #    per Subject DN) using a file as the seen-set: this is robust to
   107:     #    Subject DNs that happen to contain unusual characters which would
   108:     #    collide with an in-memory delimiter.
   109:     pool=( "${cert_files[@]}" "${ca_files[@]}" )
   110: 
   111:     SEEN="$TEMP_DIR/seen.txt"
   112:     : > "$SEEN"
   113:     : > "$OUTPUT_CHAIN"
   114:     current="$LEAF"
   115:     safety=0
   116:     while [ -n "$current" ]; do
   117:       safety=$((safety + 1))
   118:       if [ "$safety" -gt 32 ]; then
   119:         echo "ERROR: chain walk exceeded 32 hops, aborting (possible cycle)" >&2
   120:         exit 1
   121:       fi
   122: 
   123:       c_subj=$(subj_of "$current")
   124:       c_iss=$(iss_of "$current")
   125: 
   126:       if ! grep -Fxq -- "$c_subj" "$SEEN"; then
   127:         cat "$current" >> "$OUTPUT_CHAIN"
   128:         printf '%s\n' "$c_subj" >> "$SEEN"
   129:       fi
   130: 
   131:       # Self-signed -> a trust anchor, stop walking.
   132:       if [ "$c_subj" = "$c_iss" ]; then
   133:         break
   134:       fi
   135: 
   136:       # Find parent in the pool (Subject == Issuer of current cert).
   137:       parent=""
   138:       for f in "${pool[@]}"; do
   139:         [ "$f" = "$current" ] && continue
   140:         if [ "$(subj_of "$f")" = "$c_iss" ]; then
   141:           parent="$f"
   142:           break
   143:         fi
   144:       done
   145: 
   146:       # No parent found -> partial chain, stop here.
   147:       [ -z "$parent" ] && break
   148:       current="$parent"
   149:     done
   150: 
   151:     echo "Chain written to $OUTPUT_CHAIN" >&2
   152:   args:
   153:     executable: "{{ shell_executable }}"
   154:   register: build_chain_result
   155:   changed_when: build_chain_result.rc == 0
   156: 
   157: - name: Cleanup Temp Directory
   158:   file:
   159:     path: "{{ temp_dir.path }}"
   160:     state: absent
   161:   changed_when: false

    17: ---
    18: - apt:
    19:     name: delphix-virtualization
    20:     state: present
    21: 
    22: - file:
    23:     path: /var/opt/delphix
    24:     state: directory
    25: 
    26: #
    27: # The section below deals with disabling and masking services that need to be
    28: # disabled on initial install. Some of those services will remain disabled
    29: # forever, while others could be enabled by the various applications running
    30: # on the Delphix Appliance.
    31: #
    32: # Our approach is to mask services that need to be disabled. Masking a service
    33: # instead of just disabling it has 2 advantages:
    34: #  1. A service that is just disabled will not be started automatically by
    35: #     systemd on boot, however it can be started by another service if it has
    36: #     a certain set of dependencies on it (such as "Requires", "PartOf"). A
    37: #     service that is masked cannot be started in any case (although a
    38: #     service that is already running and has just been masked will not be
    39: #     stopped automatically).
    40: #  2. A service that is disabled can get re-enabled by dpkg maintenance scripts
    41: #     when the package that provides that service is upgraded. A service that
    42: #     is masked will not be unmasked.
    43: #
    44: # While masking a service is sufficient, we also disable most of the services
    45: # that we mask. This is not strictly necessary, but is done to remain
    46: # consistent with how we did things in the past. Our current logic that deals
    47: # with re-enabling those services will both unmask and enable # them.
    48: #
    49: # We have divided the disabling and masking of the services in multiple
    50: # code blocks to group together services that are handled in the same way by
    51: # the appliance.
    52: #
    53: # Note that if you want to modify this list make sure to also update
    54: # the logic in fix_and_migrate_services() that is invoked during upgrade.
    55: # You may also want to look at the logic that handles enabling disabling
    56: # services in dlpx-app-gate.
    57: #
    58: 
    59: #
    60: # The services in this section should always remain disabled & masked.
    61: #
    62: - name: Disable and mask services that should never run
    63:   shell: |
    64:     systemctl disable {{ item }}
    65:     systemctl mask {{ item }}
    66:   with_items:
    67:     - fluentd.service
    68:     - nginx.service
    69:     - postgresql.service
    70:     - telegraf.service
    71:     - influxdb.service
    72: 
    73: #
    74: # The services in this section should be disabled & masked initially, but
    75: # can be later dynamically enabled by the appliance.
    76: #
    77: # delphix-fluentd.service and delphix-masking.service are owned by the
    78: # delphix-masking package, which isn't installed on variants (DCT, UCF)
    79: # that don't include the masking-common role; "disable" on a unit that
    80: # doesn't exist fails, so it's allowed to fail here. "mask" always
    81: # succeeds regardless of whether the unit exists.
    82: #
    83: - name: Disable and mask services that should not be running by default
    84:   shell: |
    85:     systemctl disable {{ item }} || true
    86:     systemctl mask {{ item }}
    87:   with_items:
    88:     - delphix-fluentd.service
    89:     - delphix-masking.service
    90:     - chrony.service
    91:     - snmpd.service
    92: 
    93: #
    94: # Because we want an NFSv4-only configuration out of the box, we need to mask
    95: # NFSv3 services so that they don't get automatically started at boot via
    96: # dependencies. The virtualization software is responsible for unmasking and
    97: # starting these services if NFSv3 needed at runtime.
    98: #
    99: - name: Mask NFSv3 services that should not be started automatically
   100:   command: "systemctl mask {{ item }}"
   101:   with_items:
   102:     - rpcbind.service
   103:     - rpcbind.socket
   104:     - rpc-statd.service
   105: 
   106: #
   107: # We disable docker. Instead of being started automatically by systemd, it
   108: # gets started via a dependency of delphix-virtualization.
   109: #
   110: - name: Disable docker
   111:   command: "systemctl disable {{ item }}"
   112:   with_items:
   113:     - docker.service

name: roles/vdi_local_routes/tasks/main.yml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Keep internal networks reachable from a VDI guest that runs a VPN client.
     3: #
     4: # A full-tunnel client (FortiClient, and every other one) installs its own
     5: # default route when it connects. From that moment the guest's REPLY packets to
     6: # anything off its own subnet leave through the tunnel and never arrive: an
     7: # established RDP session drops, and every subsequent WinRM converge fails,
     8: # because inbound still reaches the guest while the return path is gone.
     9: #
    10: # A more-specific persistent route per preserved subnet outranks the tunnel's
    11: # default route — including the two-half variant clients often install instead
    12: # of a literal default — so those networks stay on the LAN and everything else
    13: # still goes to the VPN.
    14: #
    15: # Deliberately NOT every private range: a corporate network behind the VPN very
    16: # often overlaps the estate's own private space, and routing that past the
    17: # tunnel would break the resource the VDI exists to reach. Only the subnets
    18: # named by vdi_preserved_vlans move.
    19: 
    20: - name: Fail when the split-tunnel inputs are missing
    21:   # An empty list here is the silent-no-op shape this repo keeps getting bitten
    22:   # by: the play goes green, the operator believes the standard is applied, and
    23:   # the guest drops off the network the next time the VPN connects. A guest in
    24:   # vdi_group has asked for this standard, so absent inputs are a broken
    25:   # inventory, not an opt-out.
    26:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    27:     that:
    28:       - vdi_local_routes_destinations | length > 0
    29:       - vdi_local_routes_gateway | length > 0
    30:     fail_msg: >-
    31:       {{ inventory_hostname }} is in vdi_group but the published inventory
    32:       carries no split-tunnel inputs (destinations:
    33:       {{ vdi_local_routes_destinations | length }}, gateway present:
    34:       {{ vdi_local_routes_gateway | length > 0 }}). Set vdi_preserved_vlans in
    35:       deployment.json and re-run the tofu-proxmox workspace so the inventory
    36:       republishes with vdi_preserved_cidrs and a per-VM gateway.
    37: 
    38: - name: Pin the preserved subnets to the LAN gateway
    39:   # Both policy stores, deliberately. ActiveStore takes effect now; only
    40:   # PersistentStore survives a reboot, and a route that vanishes on the next
    41:   # restart is worse than none — it works when tested and fails unattended.
    42:   # A route whose next hop no longer matches the published gateway is replaced
    43:   # rather than left alongside, so a VLAN renumber converges instead of
    44:   # accumulating a dead entry that still wins on prefix length.
    45:   #
    46:   # win_powershell, not win_shell: win_shell is free-form, so Ansible splits the
    47:   # script as module arguments and this one does not survive it ("unbalanced
    48:   # jinja2 block or quotes" — caught by ansible-lint). Passing the values as
    49:   # typed parameters also keeps Jinja out of the PowerShell entirely.
    50:   ansible.windows.win_powershell:
    51:     parameters:
    52:       Destination: "{{ item }}"
    53:       Gateway: "{{ vdi_local_routes_gateway }}"
    54:       Metric: "{{ vdi_local_routes_metric }}"
    55:     script: |
    56:       param([string]$Destination, [string]$Gateway, [int]$Metric)
    57:       $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
    58: 
    59:       # Resolve the interface that actually reaches the gateway. The gateway sits
    60:       # on the guest's own subnet, which stays on-link even with the tunnel up,
    61:       # so this returns the physical NIC rather than the VPN adapter.
    62:       $ifIndex = (Find-NetRoute -RemoteIPAddress $Gateway -ErrorAction Stop |
    63:                   Select-Object -First 1).InterfaceIndex
    64: 
    65:       # `route -p add`, not New-NetRoute -PolicyStore PersistentStore. The
    66:       # cmdlet rejects the persistent store on this build with "Invalid
    67:       # parameter PolicyStore PersistentStore" (Windows System Error 87) using
    68:       # EITHER -InterfaceIndex or -InterfaceAlias — both were tried against a
    69:       # live guest. Its index form DOES succeed against ActiveStore, which is
    70:       # the dangerous shape: the live route is written, the persistent write
    71:       # errors, and the route disappears at the next reboot. That is precisely
    72:       # the failure this role exists to prevent, and it would read as working.
    73:       #
    74:       # route.exe -p writes the live route AND the registry persistent route in
    75:       # one operation, so the two cannot diverge.
    76:       $parts = $Destination -split '/'
    77:       $network = $parts[0]
    78:       $len = [int]$parts[1]
    79:       $octets = @(0, 0, 0, 0)
    80:       for ($i = 0; $i -lt 4; $i++) {
    81:         $bits = [Math]::Min(8, [Math]::Max(0, $len - ($i * 8)))
    82:         $octets[$i] = [byte](256 - [Math]::Pow(2, 8 - $bits))
    83:       }
    84:       $mask = $octets -join '.'

    86:       $live = @(Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix $Destination -PolicyStore ActiveStore `
    87:                              -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    88:                 Where-Object { $_.NextHop -eq $Gateway })
    89:       # Check the POLICY STORE, not the legacy
    90:       # Tcpip\Parameters\PersistentRoutes registry key. `route -p add` on this

    92:       # testing the registry finds nothing every time and the task re-adds an
    93:       # already-correct route and reports changed on every converge — verified
    94:       # against the live guest, where the routes were present in the store while
    95:       # the key held nothing at all.
    96:       $persisted = @(Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix $Destination `
    97:                                   -PolicyStore PersistentStore `
    98:                                   -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    99:                      Where-Object { $_.NextHop -eq $Gateway })

   101:       $changed = $false
   102:       if (-not $live -or -not $persisted) {

   104:         # destination via a dead next hop still wins on prefix length and would
   105:         # black-hole the traffic this role is protecting.
   106:         # route.exe writes "Element not found" to STDERR when there is nothing
   107:         # to delete, and with ErrorActionPreference = Stop PowerShell promotes
   108:         # any native stderr to a terminating NativeCommandError — so the
   109:         # clean-up step fails the task in the ordinary case where the route was
   110:         # simply absent. Nothing to delete is a success here, so drop the
   111:         # preference for exactly this call.
   112:         $prev = $ErrorActionPreference
   113:         $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
   114:         & route delete $network mask $mask 2>&1 | Out-Null
   115:         $ErrorActionPreference = $prev
   116: 
   117:         $out = & route -p add $network mask $mask $Gateway metric $Metric if $ifIndex 2>&1
   118:         if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "route -p add failed (rc=$LASTEXITCODE): $out" }

   120:       }
   121: 
   122:       # win_powershell reports changed unless told otherwise, so a converge that
   123:       # altered nothing would still read as a change on every run.
   124:       $Ansible.Changed = $changed
   125:   loop: "{{ vdi_local_routes_destinations }}"

    10:         path: "{{ postgres_backup_dir }}"

    26:         src: pg-backup.service.j2
    27:         dest: /etc/systemd/system/pg-backup.service
    28:         owner: root
    29:         group: root
    30:         mode: "0644"
    31: 
    32:     - name: Deploy the pg_dump backup systemd timer
    33:       ansible.builtin.template:
    34:         src: pg-backup.timer.j2
    35:         dest: /etc/systemd/system/pg-backup.timer
    36:         owner: root
    37:         group: root
    38:         mode: "0644"
    39: 
    40:     - name: Enable and start the pg_dump backup timer
    41:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
    42:         name: pg-backup.timer
    43:         state: started
    44:         enabled: true
    45:         daemon_reload: true
    46: 
    47: # Trust the standby node's puller so ansible-proxmox roles/postgres_standby can
    48: # rsync the backup directory into the replicated archive (Tier 1 of the
    49: # Database DR Standard). Env-gated: no key supplied, no trust installed.
    50: #
    51: # rrsync is the forced command rather than a pinned `rsync --server --sender`
    52: # argv: the argv the client sends changes with rsync's flags, so pinning it
    53: # breaks the pull silently on an upgrade. rrsync ships in the rsync package.
    54: #
    55: # Both tasks also carry their own tag so the trust can be (re)applied on its
    56: # own — rotating a puller's key should not require converging the whole
    57: # engine on a live database guest:
    58: #
    59: #   --tags postgres_standby_trust -e postgres_standby_pull_pubkeys="$(...)"
    60: #
    61: # Pass the keys as an EXTRA VAR, not an exported environment variable.
    62: # `VAR=x doppler run -- ...` does not override a Doppler-managed variable —
    63: # Doppler's injected value wins over the caller's export, silently — so an
    64: # export is ignored and whatever the secret holds is authorized instead, at
    65: # rc=0 with changed=true. The default binding no longer reads any env var
    66: # (it fed the stale pve2 puller key on every converge); an extra var is the
    67: # only resolution path.
    68: - name: Install rsync for the standby puller's forced command
    69:   ansible.builtin.apt:
    70:     name: rsync
    71:     state: present
    72:   when: postgres_standby_pull_pubkeys | length > 0
    73:   tags:
    74:     - postgres_standby_trust
    75: 
    76: - name: Authorize the standby puller's SSH key(s) for root
    77:   ansible.posix.authorized_key:
    78:     user: root
    79:     key: "{{ postgres_standby_pull_pubkeys }}"
    80:     # The puller anchors its source path at "/" — rrsync resolves that to this
    81:     # directory. An absolute path would be prefixed with it and match nothing.
    82:     key_options: 'restrict,command="rrsync -ro {{ postgres_backup_dir }}"'
    83:   when: postgres_standby_pull_pubkeys | length > 0
    84:   tags:
    85:     - postgres_standby_trust
    86: 
    87: # Declared state includes the absence: the decommissioned pve2 puller's key
    88: # (forced rrsync command, comment root@pve2) was re-authorised by every
    89: # converge while the env binding above still fed the stale Doppler secret
    90: # (Zammad #17250). Not gated on pubkeys — this scrubs even when no puller is
    91: # being trusted, and matches only that puller's line so human and current
    92: # puller keys are untouched. The current pullers' keys carry the
    93: # postgres-standby-pull comment instead.
    94: - name: Remove trust for the decommissioned pve2 backup puller
    95:   ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
    96:     path: /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
    97:     regexp: 'rrsync -ro .*\broot@pve2$'
    98:     state: absent
    99:   tags:
   100:     - postgres_standby_trust

review_question: Is this Ansible artifact excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Vikunja native install. The controller stages the checksum-verified release
     3: # bundle (LXCs here are firewalled outbound-internal-only and cannot reach
     4: # GitHub), extracts the single binary, and copies it to the target — same
     5: # controller-staging pattern as roles/openbao and roles/technitium_install.
     6: 
     7: - name: Validate Vikunja secrets are set
     8:   ansible.builtin.assert:
     9:     that:
    10:       - vikunja_db_password | length > 0
    11:       - vikunja_jwt_secret | length > 0
    12:       - vikunja_admin_password | length > 0
    13:     fail_msg: >-
    14:       VIKUNJA_DB_PASSWORD / VIKUNJA_JWT_SECRET / VIKUNJA_ADMIN_PASSWORD must
    15:       all be set before first deploy. Add via: doppler secrets set
    16:       VIKUNJA_DB_PASSWORD=<password> VIKUNJA_JWT_SECRET=<secret>
    17:       VIKUNJA_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<password>
    18:     quiet: true
    19:   no_log: true
    20: 
    21: - name: Create vikunja system group
    22:   ansible.builtin.group:
    23:     name: "{{ vikunja_group }}"
    24:     system: true
    25:     state: present
    26: 
    27: - name: Create vikunja system user
    28:   ansible.builtin.user:
    29:     name: "{{ vikunja_user }}"
    30:     group: "{{ vikunja_group }}"
    31:     system: true
    32:     shell: /usr/sbin/nologin
    33:     home: "{{ vikunja_install_dir }}"
    34:     create_home: false
    35:     state: present
    36: 
    37: - name: Create Vikunja directories
    38:   ansible.builtin.file:
    39:     path: "{{ item.path }}"
    40:     state: directory
    41:     owner: "{{ item.owner }}"
    42:     group: "{{ vikunja_group }}"
    43:     mode: "{{ item.mode }}"
    44:   loop:
    45:     - { path: "{{ vikunja_install_dir }}", owner: root, mode: "0755" }
    46:     - { path: "{{ vikunja_config_dir }}", owner: root, mode: "0750" }
    47:     - { path: "{{ vikunja_files_dir }}", owner: "{{ vikunja_user }}", mode: "0750" }
    48:   loop_control:
    49:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
    50: 
    51: # ansible_become: false on the delegated tasks is REQUIRED — Ansible inherits
    52: # the play's become: true on delegated tasks regardless of task-level become,
    53: # which fails with "sudo: a password is required" on the controller.
    54: - name: Stage the Vikunja release bundle on controller (checksum-verified)
    55:   ansible.builtin.get_url:
    56:     url: "{{ vikunja_release_zip_url }}"
    57:     dest: "/tmp/{{ vikunja_release_zip }}"
    58:     checksum: "sha256:{{ vikunja_release_zip_sha256 }}"
    59:     mode: "0644"
    60:     force: true
    61:   delegate_to: localhost
    62:   connection: local
    63:   become: false
    64:   vars:
    65:     ansible_become: false
    66:   run_once: true
    67: 
    68: - name: Extract the Vikunja binary on controller
    69:   ansible.builtin.unarchive:
    70:     src: "/tmp/{{ vikunja_release_zip }}"
    71:     dest: /tmp
    72:     remote_src: true
    73:     include:
    74:       - "{{ vikunja_binary_name }}"
    75:     # unarchive re-extracts (and reports changed) every run without this guard;
    76:     # the zip is checksum-pinned, so an existing extract is always current.
    77:     creates: "/tmp/{{ vikunja_binary_name }}"
    78:   delegate_to: localhost
    79:   connection: local
    80:   become: false
    81:   vars:
    82:     ansible_become: false
    83:   run_once: true
    84: 
    85: - name: Copy the Vikunja binary to the target
    86:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    87:     src: "/tmp/{{ vikunja_binary_name }}"
    88:     dest: "{{ vikunja_binary_path }}"
    89:     owner: root
    90:     group: root
    91:     mode: "0755"
    92:   notify: Restart vikunja
    93: 
    94: - name: Render Vikunja config
    95:   ansible.builtin.template:
    96:     src: config.yml.j2
    97:     dest: "{{ vikunja_config_file }}"
    98:     owner: root
    99:     group: "{{ vikunja_group }}"
   100:     mode: "0640"
   101:   notify: Restart vikunja
   102: 
   103: - name: Install the vikunja systemd unit
   104:   ansible.builtin.template:
   105:     src: vikunja.service.j2
   106:     dest: /etc/systemd/system/vikunja.service
   107:     owner: root
   108:     group: root
   109:     mode: "0644"
   110:   notify: Restart vikunja
   111: 
   112: - name: Enable and start Vikunja
   113:   ansible.builtin.systemd:
   114:     name: vikunja
   115:     state: started
   116:     enabled: true
   117:     daemon_reload: true
   118: 
   119: # Flush so a config/unit/binary change is live before the health check and
   120: # CLI user-management tasks below run against it.
   121: - name: Apply any pending Vikunja restart
   122:   ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers
   123: 
   124: - name: Wait for Vikunja to answer its info endpoint
   125:   ansible.builtin.uri:
   126:     url: "http://localhost:{{ vikunja_port }}/api/v1/info"
   127:     method: GET
   128:     status_code: [200]
   129:     timeout: "{{ vikunja_api_timeout }}"
   130:   register: vikunja_health
   131:   until: vikunja_health.status == 200
   132:   retries: 10
   133:   delay: 3
   134:   changed_when: false
   135: 
   136: # `vikunja user list` needs no --config flag — the CLI shares the server's
   137: # config auto-discovery (rootpath -> /etc/vikunja/ -> ~/.config/vikunja -> .),
   138: # and /etc/vikunja/ is always searched regardless of cwd.
   139: - name: List existing Vikunja users
   140:   ansible.builtin.command:
   141:     argv:
   142:       - "{{ vikunja_binary_path }}"
   143:       - user
   144:       - list
   145:   register: vikunja_user_list
   146:   changed_when: false
   147: 
   148: - name: Create the Vikunja admin user (idempotent — skipped if already present)
   149:   ansible.builtin.command:
   150:     argv:
   151:       - "{{ vikunja_binary_path }}"
   152:       - user
   153:       - create
   154:       - "--username={{ vikunja_admin_user }}"
   155:       - "--email={{ vikunja_admin_email }}"
   156:       - "--password={{ vikunja_admin_password }}"
   157:   # Match the exact username as a whole table cell in `vikunja user list`
   158:   # output. A `\b` word boundary is wrong here: `-` is a non-word char, so
   159:   # `\badmin\b` would match "admin" inside "admin-helper". Anchor on
   160:   # start/whitespace/pipe (the table delimiters) instead. `default('', true)`
   161:   # guards against an undefined stdout when the list task is skipped.
   162:   when: >-
   163:     not (vikunja_user_list.stdout | default('', true)
   164:          | regex_search('(?:^|\\s|\\|)' ~ vikunja_admin_user ~ '(?:\\s|\\||$)'))
   165:   changed_when: true
   166:   no_log: true
   167: 
   168: - name: Create Vikunja service users (idempotent — skipped if already present)
   169:   ansible.builtin.command:
   170:     argv:
   171:       - "{{ vikunja_binary_path }}"
   172:       - user
   173:       - create
   174:       - "--username={{ item.username }}"
   175:       - "--email={{ item.username }}@{{ tofu_data.domain }}"
   176:       - "--password={{ item.password }}"
   177:   loop: "{{ vikunja_service_users }}"
   178:   loop_control:
   179:     label: "{{ item.username }}"
   180:   # Whole-cell match (see the admin task above): a `\b` boundary would let
   181:   # `svc-mcp-ro` false-match inside a hypothetical `svc-mcp-ro-x` and skip
   182:   # a real creation.
   183:   when:
   184:     - item.password | length > 0
   185:     - >-
   186:       not (vikunja_user_list.stdout | default('', true)
   187:            | regex_search('(?:^|\\s|\\|)' ~ item.username ~ '(?:\\s|\\||$)'))
   188:   changed_when: true
   189:   no_log: true
   190: 
   191: - name: Create the Vikunja operator user (idempotent — skipped if already present)
   192:   ansible.builtin.command:
   193:     argv:
   194:       - "{{ vikunja_binary_path }}"
   195:       - user
   196:       - create
   197:       - "--username={{ vikunja_operator_username }}"
   198:       - "--email={{ vikunja_operator_email }}"
   199:       - "--password={{ vikunja_operator_password }}"
   200:   # Whole-cell match, same reasoning as the admin/service-user tasks above.
   201:   when:
   202:     - vikunja_operator_username | length > 0
   203:     - vikunja_operator_password | length > 0
   204:     - >-
   205:       not (vikunja_user_list.stdout | default('', true)
   206:            | regex_search('(?:^|\\s|\\|)' ~ vikunja_operator_username ~ '(?:\\s|\\||$)'))
   207:   changed_when: true
   208:   no_log: true
   209: 
   210: # Share every project the automation accounts own with the operator. Vikunja
   211: # projects are per-owner with no super-user override, so without this the
   212: # operator logs in to an empty board list. Additive only — the owning accounts
   213: # keep ownership and access.
   214: - name: Grant the operator access to the automation-owned projects
   215:   ansible.builtin.include_tasks: operator_access.yml
   216:   when:
   217:     - vikunja_operator_username | length > 0
   218:     - vikunja_operator_password | length > 0
   219:     - not ansible_check_mode
   220:   tags: vikunja_operator_access
   221: 
   222: # ansible.builtin.uri has no check-mode support, so every request in the share
   223: # reconciliation would be skipped and the facts derived from them left
   224: # undefined. Skipping the include outright and saying so is honest; running it
   225: # half-evaluated would fail on undefined vars and prove nothing.
   226: - name: Note operator project sharing is not evaluated in check mode
   227:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   228:     msg: >-
   229:       Operator project sharing is skipped in check mode (ansible.builtin.uri
   230:       does not support it). Run without --check to reconcile the operator's
   231:       share on the automation-owned projects.
   232:   when:
   233:     - vikunja_operator_username | length > 0
   234:     - vikunja_operator_password | length > 0
   235:     - ansible_check_mode
   236:   tags: vikunja_operator_access
   237: 
   238: - name: Note operator account provisioning is skipped
   239:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   240:     msg: >-
   241:       Vikunja operator provisioning is skipped — DEFAULT_USERNAME and/or
   242:       DEFAULT_PASSWORD are absent from the converge environment. Set both to
   243:       create the human account and share the automation-owned projects with it.
   244:   when: not (vikunja_operator_username | length > 0 and vikunja_operator_password | length > 0)
   245: 
   246: # Mint per-user MCP API tokens and publish the shared connection to OpenBao.
   247: # Deferred by default: the converge flips the flag with
   248: # -e '{"vikunja_token_publish_openbao": true}' once a write-capable OpenBao
   249: # AppRole (BAO_ADDR/BAO_TOKEN) is in the controller environment.
   250: - name: Mint MCP API tokens and publish to OpenBao
   251:   ansible.builtin.include_tasks: mcp_tokens.yml
   252:   when: vikunja_token_publish_openbao | bool
   253:   tags: vikunja_mcp_tokens
   254: 
   255: - name: Note MCP token minting is deferred
   256:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   257:     msg: >-
   258:       Vikunja MCP token minting is deferred (vikunja_token_publish_openbao is
   259:       off). Service users exist; enable with
   260:       -e '{"vikunja_token_publish_openbao": true}' plus a write-capable OpenBao

   262:       {{ vikunja_url_openbao_key }} + per-tier tokens to
   263:       {{ vikunja_token_openbao_mount }}/{{ vikunja_token_openbao_path }}.
   264:   when: not (vikunja_token_publish_openbao | bool)

     2: # Apply the david_igou.routeros_configuration.configure role to a routeros
     3: # device using its host_vars/group_vars declarative baseline (the curated
     4: # routeros_config dict). This is the canonical apply playbook — paths flow
     5: # in through Ansible's normal var precedence, NOT sliced from a capture file.
     6: #
     7: # To preview without applying:
     8: #   ansible-playbook playbooks/routeros/configure.yaml \
     9: #     -i ../igou-inventory/inventory.yaml -e host=routeros --check
    10: # To apply:
    11: #   same command without --check.
    12: # A check-mode run (the AAP routeros_configure_check template) additionally
    13: # publishes drift_label ('clean'|'drift') and drift_summary as job artifacts,
    14: # so an Automation Orchestrator workflow can branch on the audit result. See
    15: # the post_tasks at the bottom.
    16: # To ship a fresh S3 backup snapshot before the apply touches anything
    17: # (the AAP routeros_configure template sets this):
    18: #   ... -e routeros_pre_apply_backup=true
    19: #
    20: # Graduating new paths / onboarding a new device: see
    21: # playbooks/routeros/configure_from_capture.yaml (capture-file harness),
    22: # then append proven path blocks to igou-inventory/host_vars/<host>.yml and
    23: # re-run this playbook in --check to confirm idempotency.
    24: 
    25: # Opt-in pre-apply backup: chains backup_s3.yaml so a fresh snapshot pair
    26: # (.rsc + binary) lands in S3 before configure writes. Recovery from a bad
    27: # apply is the normal restore path (fetch from S3, /import or
    28: # /system backup load). Tier stays 'daily' so the snapshot ages out under
    29: # the same lifecycle rule as scheduled backups.
    30: - name: Pre-apply S3 backup (opt-in via routeros_pre_apply_backup)
    31:   ansible.builtin.import_playbook: backup_s3.yaml
    32:   vars:
    33:     # Align backup_s3.yaml's default host (routeros, whole group) with this
    34:     # playbook's default (routeros_router). `-e host=<x>` on the CLI
    35:     # overrides this literal — extra-vars beat play vars.
    36:     host: routeros_router
    37:   when: routeros_pre_apply_backup | default(false) | bool
    38: 
    39: - name: Configure RouterOS device from declarative host_vars baseline
    40:   hosts: "{{ host | default('routeros_router') }}"
    41:   gather_facts: false
    42: 
    43:   vars:
    44:     routeros_api_tls: true
    45:     routeros_api_validate_certs: false
    46:     routeros_api_port: 8729
    47: 
    48:   handlers:
    49:     # Notified (via the `apply:` below) by every task the role runs that
    50:     # reports changed. In CHECK mode nothing was written, so "changed" means
    51:     # "the device does not match the baseline" — that is the drift signal the
    52:     # role otherwise does not expose. In apply mode this only records that a
    53:     # write happened; nothing reads it.
    54:     - name: Record that the baseline reported a change
    55:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    56:         rcfg_changed: true
    57: 
    58:   pre_tasks:
    59:     - name: Resolve api-ssl credentials once
    60:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    61:         routeros_api_username: "{{ routeros_api_credentials.username }}"
    62:         routeros_api_password: "{{ routeros_api_credentials.password }}"

    71:           No routeros_config baseline found for {{ inventory_hostname }}. Add

    73:           equivalent) before running configure.
    74: 
    75:   tasks:
    76:     # Was a `roles:` entry. It is an include_role purely so `apply:` can attach
    77:     # `notify:` to every task the role runs — including the nested _reconcile
    78:     # includes, which is where api_modify actually reports changed. Execution
    79:     # position (after pre_tasks, before post_tasks), role arguments, and module
    80:     # arguments are all unchanged, so apply-mode behavior is unchanged.

    82:       ansible.builtin.include_role:
    83:         name: david_igou.routeros_configuration.configure

    90:   # Check mode only: publish the drift verdict as orchestrator artifacts

   100:           drift_summary: "{{ _summary[:4000] }}"

   102:         aggregate: false

   107:              | map(attribute='inventory_hostname') | list }}

Run the routeros_configure job template to converge the device, or update host_vars if the device is the source of truth; this job's diff output carries the per-path detail.{% else %}The device already matches its host_vars baseline exactly.{% endif %}

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Measure disk utilization on one mount and publish structured artifacts for
     3: # the automation orchestrator disk-utilization workflow (AAP template:
     4: # disk_check). The orchestrator's switch node routes on disk_use_percent /
     5: # disk_tier; see igou-docs "AO Artifacts for Structured Output".
     6: #
     7: # Targeting: pass ansible_limit=<host> (defaults to 'none' — never 'all').
     8: # Single-host runs only: set_stats artifacts are workflow-scoped, so a
     9: # multi-host limit would clobber per-host values. The orchestrator loops
    10: # hosts by launching one job per host.
    11: #
    12: # Variables:
    13: #   disk_mount - mount point to measure (default '/')
    14: #
    15: # Artifacts (set_stats -> AAP job artifacts -> orchestrator step output):
    16: #   disk_host, disk_mount, disk_use_percent (int), disk_tier
    17: #   (healthy|warning|critical), disk_detail (top space consumers, text)
    18: - name: Check disk utilization and publish tier artifacts
    19:   hosts: "{{ ansible_limit | default('none') }}"
    20:   become: true
    21:   gather_facts: true
    22:   vars:
    23:     disk_mount: /
    24:     disk_warn_percent: 80
    25:     disk_crit_percent: 95
    26:   tasks:
    27:     - name: Locate the requested mount in gathered facts
    28:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    29:         disk_mount_info: >-
    30:           {{ ansible_facts.mounts | selectattr('mount', 'equalto', disk_mount) | first }}
    31: 
    32:     - name: Compute utilization percentage
    33:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    34:         disk_use_percent: >-
    35:           {{ (100 - (disk_mount_info.size_available * 100 / disk_mount_info.size_total)) | round(0, 'ceil') | int }}
    36: 
    37:     - name: Classify tier
    38:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    39:         disk_tier: >-
    40:           {{ 'critical' if disk_use_percent | int > disk_crit_percent
    41:              else 'warning' if disk_use_percent | int >= disk_warn_percent
    42:              else 'healthy' }}
    43: 
    44:     - name: Collect top space consumers under /var (for the summary step)
    45:       ansible.builtin.shell:
    46:         cmd: set -o pipefail; du -xm --max-depth=2 /var 2>/dev/null | sort -rn | head -12
    47:         executable: /bin/bash
    48:       register: disk_du
    49:       changed_when: false
    50:       failed_when: false
    51: 
    52:     - name: Publish artifacts for the orchestrator
    53:       ansible.builtin.set_stats:
    54:         data:
    55:           disk_host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
    56:           disk_mount: "{{ disk_mount }}"
    57:           disk_use_percent: "{{ disk_use_percent | int }}"
    58:           disk_tier: "{{ disk_tier }}"
    59:           disk_detail: "{{ disk_du.stdout | default('unavailable') }}"
    60:         per_host: false
    61: 
    62:     - name: Report

1: ---
     2: # Gateway collector — OpenTelemetry-recommended "gateway pattern" implementation.
     3: # Called from setup.yml when `opentelemetry_gateway_enabled: true`, *before*
     4: # the helm task so the gateway collector spec AND its supporting resources
     5: # (htpasswd Secret + Ingress) are included in the chart values.
     6: #
     7: # All resources go through helm via:
     8: #   - `collectors.<gateway_name>` (the OpenTelemetryCollector CR + the
     9: #     operator-spawned Service/Deployment) → driven by
    10: #     `opentelemetry_collectors[<gateway_name>]`
    11: #   - `extraObjects[]` (Secret + Ingress) → driven by
    12: #     `opentelemetry_additional_config.extraObjects`
    13: #
    14: # That way helm owns the full lifecycle: a `helm upgrade` after disabling
    15: # the gateway tears everything down, and credential rotation is reflected
    16: # through a pod-annotation checksum so the operator triggers a rollout.
    17: 
    18: - name: "Compute gateway derived values"
    19:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    20:     _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}"
    21:     _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}-htpasswd"
    22:     _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled: "{{ (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | default('') | length) > 0 }}"
    23: 
    24: - name: "Build the gateway collector spec"
    25:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    26:     opentelemetry_collectors: >-
    27:       {{
    28:         (opentelemetry_collectors | default({}))
    29:         | combine({ opentelemetry_gateway_name: _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec }, recursive=True)
    30:       }}
    31:   vars:
    32:     _volumes: >-
    33:       {{
    34:         [{
    35:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    36:           'secret': {'secretName': _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name}
    37:         }]
    38:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    39:       }}
    40:     _volume_mounts: >-
    41:       {{
    42:         [{
    43:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    44:           'mountPath': '/etc/otel-auth',
    45:           'readOnly': true
    46:         }]
    47:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    48:       }}
    49:     # Credential rotation: the basicauth/server extension caches the
    50:     # htpasswd file at startup, so secret content changes only take effect
    51:     # when the pod restarts. Putting a checksum of the content in
    52:     # podAnnotations makes the operator roll the pod whenever the content
    53:     # differs from the previous apply.
    54:     _pod_annotations: >-
    55:       {{
    56:         {'checksum/htpasswd': (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | hash('sha256'))}
    57:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    58:       }}
    59:     _extensions: >-
    60:       {{
    61:         {'basicauth/server': {'htpasswd': {'file': '/etc/otel-auth/htpasswd'}}}
    62:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    63:       }}
    64:     _service_extensions: >-
    65:       {{
    66:         ['basicauth/server']
    67:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    68:       }}
    69:     # Auto-wire basicauth/server onto the OTLP HTTP receiver. We deep-merge
    70:     # so the user keeps full control of receiver options (compression,
    71:     # max_recv_msg_size, …).
    72:     _otlp_http_auth_overlay:
    73:       otlp:
    74:         protocols:
    75:           http:
    76:             auth:
    77:               authenticator: "basicauth/server"
    78:     _receivers: >-
    79:       {{
    80:         opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    81:         | combine(_otlp_http_auth_overlay, recursive=True)
    82:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled
    83:         else opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    84:       }}
    85:     # If the user did not provide explicit pipelines, route every receiver +
    86:     # processor + exporter into metrics & logs pipelines. Works for the
    87:     # common case of homogeneous OTLP exporters; override when you have
    88:     # signal-specific routing.
    89:     _default_pipelines:
    90:       metrics:
    91:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    92:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    93:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    94:       logs:
    95:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    96:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    97:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    98:     _pipelines: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines if (opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines | length > 0) else _default_pipelines }}"
    99:     _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec:

   101:       mode: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_mode }}"
   102:       replicas: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_replicas }}"
   103:       # Predictable service name (`<release>-<gateway_name>-collector`),
   104:       # otherwise the chart defaults to `<release>-collector` which
   105:       # collides with any other non-daemon collector. Required for the
   106:       # Ingress backend reference below.
   107:       fullnameOverride: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"
   108:       resources: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_resources }}"
   109:       volumes: "{{ _volumes }}"
   110:       volumeMounts: "{{ _volume_mounts }}"
   111:       podAnnotations: "{{ _pod_annotations }}"
   112:       config:
   113:         extensions: "{{ _extensions }}"
   114:         receivers: "{{ _receivers }}"
   115:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors }}"
   116:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters }}"
   117:         service:
   118:           extensions: "{{ _service_extensions }}"
   119:           pipelines: "{{ _pipelines }}"
   120: 
   121: - name: "Inject the gateway Secret + Ingress as chart extraObjects"
   122:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   123:     opentelemetry_additional_config: >-
   124:       {{
   125:         (opentelemetry_additional_config | default({}))
   126:         | combine({
   127:             'extraObjects': (
   128:               ((opentelemetry_additional_config | default({})).extraObjects | default([]))
   129:               + _gateway_extra_objects
   130:             )
   131:           })
   132:       }}
   133:   when: _gateway_extra_objects | length > 0
   134:   vars:
   135:     _htpasswd_secret_obj:
   136:       apiVersion: "v1"
   137:       kind: "Secret"
   138:       metadata:
   139:         name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name }}"
   140:         namespace: "{{ opentelemetry_namespace }}"
   141:       type: "Opaque"
   142:       stringData:
   143:         htpasswd: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd }}"
   144:     _ingress_obj:
   145:       apiVersion: "networking.k8s.io/v1"
   146:       kind: "Ingress"
   147:       metadata:
   148:         name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"
   149:         namespace: "{{ opentelemetry_namespace }}"
   150:         annotations: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_annotations }}"
   151:       spec:
   152:         ingressClassName: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_class_name }}"
   153:         tls: >-
   154:           {{
   155:             [{
   156:               'hosts': [opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_hostname],
   157:               'secretName': opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_tls_secret_name
   158:             }]
   159:             if opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_tls_enabled else []
   160:           }}

   162:           - host: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_hostname }}"

   164:               paths:

    43: - name: Extract container images from resources
    44:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    45:     container_images_in_ns: "\
    46:       {% if resources.resource == 'Pod' %}\

    54: # Then, create the component, and that's the same for all resources.
    55: # Why we do this in this way?

    67: # * container_image_version

    71: #     else
    72: #       - use "latest" as tag

    97:         {% endfor %}\
    98:       {% endif %}"
    99:     container_image_name: "\
   100:       {% for image_chunk in container_image_without_version.split('/') %}\
   101:         {% if loop.index > 1 %}{{ image_chunk }}{% if not loop.last %}/{% endif %}{% endif %}\
   102:       {% endfor %}"
   103:     container_image_version: "\
   104:       {% if container_image.split('@') | length == 1 %}\
   105:         {% if '/' not in container_image.split(':')[-1] %}\
   106:           {{ container_image.split(':')[-1] }}\

   108:           latest
   109:         {% endif %}\
   110:       {% else %}\
   111:         {{ container_image.split('@')[-1] }}\
   112:       {% endif %}"
   113:     container_image_version_short: "\
   114:       {% if container_image_version.split(':') | length == 1 %}\
   115:         {{ container_image_version }}\
   116:       {% else %}\
   117:         {{ container_image_version.split(':')[-1][:7] }}\
   118:       {% endif %}"
   119:     comp_display_name: "IMG {{ container_image_name }} {{ container_image_version_short }}"
   120:     comp_version: "{{ container_image_version }}"
   121:     comp_type: "{{ container_image_name }}"
   122:   ansible.builtin.include_tasks: create-component.yml
   123:   loop: "{{ container_images_in_ns }}"
   124:   loop_control:
   125:     loop_var: container_image
   126: ...

1: ---
     2: # Re-pair playbook for zeroclaw restart (issue #437).
     3: #
     4: # The systemd restart itself happens in start.yaml / stop.yaml (driven by
     5: # lifecycle.restart_agent's stop -> start path). This playbook runs *after*
     6: # the daemon is back up: it waits for /health/providers to respond, then
     7: # performs the pair handshake. The new bearer token is emitted as a
     8: # cacheable host fact so lifecycle.restart_agent can persist it to
     9: # hosts.json under agents.<n>.config.gateway.auth.
    10: #
    11: # Without this step, a `clawctl agent restart zeroclaw-…` would silently
    12: # invalidate hosts.json's bearer (the daemon mints a fresh token on
    13: # startup, so the old token in hosts.json no longer matches whatever the
    14: # daemon will enforce).
    15: 
    16: # ATX W-SEC-4: no `become: yes` — every task in this play (the
    17: # /health/providers probe + the included pair.yaml handshake) hits
    18: # loopback HTTP only. Privilege escalation here would broaden blast
    19: # radius for zero benefit; if a future task needs root, add `become`
    20: # at the task level (not the play level).
    21: - hosts: all
    22:   vars:
    23:     gateway_port: "{{ config.gateway.port }}"
    24:     gateway_local_base: "http://127.0.0.1:{{ gateway_port }}"
    25:   tasks:
    26:     - name: Probe /health/providers
    27:       ansible.builtin.uri:
    28:         url: "{{ gateway_local_base }}/health/providers"
    29:         method: GET
    30:         status_code: [200, 401]
    31:         timeout: 5
    32:       register: health_probe
    33:       retries: 30
    34:       delay: 2
    35:       until: health_probe.status in [200, 401]
    36:       no_log: true
    37: 
    38:     - name: Run zeroclaw pair handshake
    39:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/pair.yaml

1: ---
     2: # ZeroClaw memory write — drops content into ~/.zeroclaw/workspace/<filename>.
     3: # The Python dispatcher applies MAX_MEMORY_CONTENT_BYTES and filename
     4: # validation before this play runs; the validators below are
     5: # defense-in-depth against a tampered inventory.
     6: #
     7: # Structural allowlist mirrors _MEMORY_WRITE_ALLOWED_FILES['zeroclaw']
     8: # (6 personality files) plus memory/<file> daily notes. BOOTSTRAP.md is
     9: # intentionally NOT writable from clawctl — the runtime owns its lifecycle.
    10: - hosts: all
    11:   become: yes
    12:   gather_facts: false
    13:   vars:
    14:     zeroclaw_writable_files:
    15:       - SOUL.md
    16:       - IDENTITY.md
    17:       - USER.md
    18:       - AGENTS.md
    19:       - TOOLS.md
    20:       - MEMORY.md
    21:   tasks:
    22:     - name: Validate agent_name (defense-in-depth)
    23:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    24:         msg: "Invalid agent_name"
    25:       when:
    26:         - agent_name is not match('^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$')
    27: 
    28:     - name: Validate memory filename pattern
    29:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    30:         msg: "Invalid memory filename"
    31:       when:
    32:         - memory_filename is not match('^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?$')
    33: 
    34:     - name: Reject path-traversal components
    35:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    36:         msg: "Invalid memory filename: traversal components not allowed"
    37:       when:
    38:         - memory_filename.split('/') | intersect(['', '.', '..']) | length > 0
    39: 
    40:     - name: Restrict to zeroclaw personality + daily-notes allowlist
    41:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    42:         msg: >-
    43:           zeroclaw memory write rejects '{{ memory_filename }}'. Allowed:
    44:           one of {{ zeroclaw_writable_files | join(', ') }}
    45:           or memory/<file>.
    46:       when:
    47:         - memory_filename not in zeroclaw_writable_files
    48:         - not (memory_filename is match('^memory/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$'))
    49: 
    50:     - name: Ensure workspace directory exists
    51:       ansible.builtin.file:
    52:         path: "/home/{{ agent_name }}/.zeroclaw/workspace"
    53:         state: directory
    54:         owner: "{{ agent_name }}"
    55:         group: "{{ agent_name }}"
    56:         mode: "0700"
    57: 
    58:     - name: Ensure memory subdirectory exists when needed
    59:       ansible.builtin.file:
    60:         path: "/home/{{ agent_name }}/.zeroclaw/workspace/memory"
    61:         state: directory
    62:         owner: "{{ agent_name }}"
    63:         group: "{{ agent_name }}"
    64:         mode: "0700"
    65:       when: memory_filename is match('^memory/.*$')
    66: 
    67:     - name: Write memory file content
    68:       # Content is passed as base64 from Python so user-supplied bytes are
    69:       # never interpreted as Jinja2. Decoding via the b64decode filter
    70:       # produces the literal payload without re-templating.
    71:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    72:         content: "{{ memory_content_b64 | b64decode }}"
    73:         dest: "/home/{{ agent_name }}/.zeroclaw/workspace/{{ memory_filename }}"
    74:         owner: "{{ agent_name }}"
    75:         group: "{{ agent_name }}"
    76:         mode: "0600"
    77:       no_log: true

     2: # Hermes workspace overlay — macOS variant (issue #772, Phase 6 of #760).
     3: # Mirrors operator-supplied files from the control-plane staging tree
     4: # onto the agent host under `workspace_dest_root` (declared in
     5: # hermes/manifest.yaml).
     6: #
     7: # The macOS playbook mirrors workspace.yaml's task structure with two
     8: # OS-specific deltas:
     9: #   (a) home-dir root is `/Users/<agent_name>/`, not `/home/<agent_name>/`
    10: #       (macOS user homes live under `/Users`).
    11: #   (b) `group: staff` is hardcoded instead of `group: "{{ agent_name }}"`
    12: #       (macOS does NOT create a per-user primary group like Linux does;
    13: #       every user's primary group is `staff` (gid 20) by default).
    14: # Reverting either delta to match Linux will fail at apply time on a
    15: # darwin host, so do not treat them as drift.
    16: #
    17: # Hermes is the only agent type with a non-empty exclude list. The
    18: # destination root `~/.hermes/` is shared with canonical-render output
    19: # (`.env`, `config.yaml`), reconciled skills under
    20: # `skills/clawrium/`, and the daemon's own SQLite state (`state.db`
    21: # + WAL companions). The exclude list reserves every one of those
    22: # paths. The Python enumerator already filters these before staging,
    23: # but this playbook re-filters per file against the exclude payload
    24: # as belt-and-suspenders so a bypass at the Python boundary cannot
    25: # overwrite renderer / daemon-managed files (hook-review S, plan U5).
    26: #
    27: # Per-file filtering is enforced via the `workspace_excluded` Jinja
    28: # filter (filter_plugins/clawrium_filters.py) — NOT via a directory-
    29: # level `find … exclude:` pattern. A directory-level pattern would let
    30: # `skills/clawrium/<sub>/SKILL.md` slip through via tree-walk shortcuts.
    31: # Ansible auto-discovers the adjacent `filter_plugins/` directory, so
    32: # the same plugin file serves both `workspace.yaml` (Linux) and this
    33: # macOS variant — no separate plugin copy required.
    34: #
    35: # The dispatcher in `core/playbook_resolver.resolve_agent_playbook`
    36: # routes to this file when `host.os_family == "darwin"` (#772).
    37: #
    38: # Inputs (extravars): same shape as workspace.yaml — see that file for
    39: # the contract. The Python side at `core/workspace_sync.py` expands
    40: # `destination_root` against `/Users/<agent_name>` for darwin hosts so
    41: # the rendered `workspace_dest_root` already begins with `/Users/...`.
    42: #
    43: # Why no `ansible_user_dir` (B1 iter-3): `become_user` does NOT re-run
    44: # the `setup` module, so `ansible_user_dir` keeps the SSH-connecting
    45: # user's home (`/Users/xclm`), not the agent user's. The literal
    46: # `/Users/{{ agent_name }}/...` pattern mirrors what
    47: # `openclaw/playbooks/workspace_macos.yaml` and
    48: # `zeroclaw/playbooks/workspace_macos.yaml` already use.

    50:   become: yes
    51:   become_user: "{{ agent_name }}"

    54:     - name: Assert agent_name matches the safe slug pattern

    56:         that:
    57:           - agent_name is string
    58:           - agent_name is match('^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$')

    60:         quiet: true

    62:     - name: Assert workspace_dest_root is under /Users/{{ agent_name }}/

    64:       # truth, but a tampered extravar pointing at e.g. `/etc/hermes`

    68:       # via path traversal — Python-side `_expand_destination_root` does

    79:           (got '{{ workspace_dest_root | default('<unset>') }}')
    80:         quiet: true

   164:       # `item.src` to an arbitrary absolute path (e.g.

   167:       # staged source lives under the asserted `staging_dir`, regardless

   176:           workspace file entry has unsafe src: '{{ item.src | default('<unset>') }}'

   188:       # handling. Mirrors openclaw/zeroclaw macOS ATX iter-1 W2.

   195:         follow: no

   197:     - name: Ensure parent directories exist for each non-excluded workspace file

   232:         # ATX iter-1 S6 (carried forward from Linux hermes/workspace.yaml):
   233:         # use `item.src` (absolute staged path computed by
   234:         # `core/workspace_sync.py:_stage_files`) rather than reconstructing

   237:         # `staging_dir / entry.rel`, but a future refactor (e.g. flattening
   238:         # or hashing staged names to dodge case-insensitive collisions on
   239:         # macOS) would silently desync these two paths if the playbook kept
   240:         # recomputing. The Python side stays the single source of truth
   241:         # for the staged source path.
   242:         src: "{{ item.src }}"
   243:         dest: "{{ workspace_dest_root }}/{{ item.rel }}"
   244:         owner: "{{ agent_name }}"
   245:         group: staff
   246:         mode: "{{ item.mode }}"
   247:         follow: no
   248:       loop: "{{ workspace_files }}"
   249:       loop_control:
   250:         label: "{{ item.rel }}"
   251:       when:
   252:         - not (item.rel | workspace_excluded(workspace_excludes_files, workspace_excludes_dirs))

     3: # Input: /mnt/tls/splunk-input-tls-cert/{tls.crt, tls.key[, ca.crt]}
     4: # Output: bundled PEM at /opt/splunk/etc/auth/input-bundle.pem

     8: - name: Generate ephemeral SSL passphrase for input cert
     9:   command: >
    10:     python3 -c
    11:     "import secrets, base64; print(base64.b64encode(secrets.token_bytes(40)).decode())"
    12:   register: input_ssl_passphrase
    13:   changed_when: false
    14:   no_log: true

    16: - name: Ensure Splunk auth directory exists

    18:     path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth"
    19:     state: directory

    21:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
    22:     mode: '0700'

    24:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"

    26: - name: Write input cert bundle script
    27:   copy:
    28:     dest: /tmp/splunk_bundle_input_cert.py
    29:     content: |
    30:       from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import (
    31:           load_pem_private_key, Encoding, PrivateFormat, BestAvailableEncryption
    32:       )
    33:       import sys
    34: 
    35:       passphrase = sys.argv[1].encode()
    36:       key_path   = '/mnt/tls/splunk-input-tls-cert/tls.key'
    37:       cert_path  = '/mnt/tls/splunk-input-tls-cert/tls.crt'
    38:       out_path   = sys.argv[2] + '/etc/auth/input-bundle.pem'
    39: 
    40:       with open(key_path, 'rb') as f:
    41:           key = load_pem_private_key(f.read(), password=None)
    42: 
    43:       enc_key_pem = key.private_bytes(
    44:           Encoding.PEM,
    45:           PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
    46:           BestAvailableEncryption(passphrase)
    47:       )
    48: 
    49:       with open(cert_path, 'rb') as f:
    50:           cert_pem = f.read()
    51: 
    52:       with open(out_path, 'wb') as f:
    53:           f.write(cert_pem)
    54:           if not cert_pem.endswith(b'\n'):
    55:               f.write(b'\n')
    56:           f.write(enc_key_pem)
    57:     mode: '0700'

    61:     python3 /tmp/splunk_bundle_input_cert.py

    90:       # tls.crt from the operator-mounted secret may contain intermediate
    91:       # certs that are not repeated in ca.crt (e.g. Vault PKI issuers put
    92:       # only the root in ca.crt). Splunk requires the full chain to be
    93:       # present locally in sslRootCAPath -- it does not complete the chain
    94:       # using intermediates presented by the peer during the handshake.
    95:       # Assemble tls.crt's non-leaf certs + ca.crt into one deduplicated
    96:       # trust bundle.
    97:       import sys
    98: 
    99:       tls_crt_path = '/mnt/tls/splunk-input-tls-cert/tls.crt'
   100:       ca_crt_path = '/mnt/tls/splunk-input-tls-cert/ca.crt'
   101:       out_path = sys.argv[1] + '/etc/auth/splunk-input-ca.pem'
   102: 
   103:       def split_pem_certs(data):
   104:           certs = []
   105:           current = []
   106:           for line in data.splitlines(keepends=True):
   107:               if line.strip() == b'-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----':
   108:                   current = [line]
   109:               elif line.strip() == b'-----END CERTIFICATE-----':
   110:                   current.append(line)
   111:                   certs.append(b''.join(current))
   112:                   current = []
   113:               elif current:
   114:                   current.append(line)
   115:           return certs
   116: 
   117:       with open(tls_crt_path, 'rb') as f:
   118:           tls_certs = split_pem_certs(f.read())
   119:       chain_certs = tls_certs[1:]  # drop the leaf; keep any presented intermediates/root
   120: 
   121:       with open(ca_crt_path, 'rb') as f:
   122:           ca_certs = split_pem_certs(f.read())
   123: 
   124:       seen = set()
   125:       ordered = []
   126:       for cert in chain_certs + ca_certs:
   127:           if cert not in seen:
   128:               seen.add(cert)
   129:               ordered.append(cert)
   130: 
   131:       with open(out_path, 'wb') as f:
   132:           for cert in ordered:
   133:               f.write(cert)
   134:               if not cert.endswith(b'\n'):
   135:                   f.write(b'\n')
   136:     mode: '0700'
